steps.text: You stand alone, gazing at the night sky. The stars call to you, whispering dreams of a future where humanity dances among them.
Ever since you were a child, you've felt it, a burning desire to lead humanity beyond Earth, to make us a spacefaring people.
But dreams alone won't get you there. You need a plan, a starting point to make this vision real.
As you ponder your next step, a letter arrives. You've been accepted to Stellaris University at the age of 18, a chance to shape your future.
What major will you pursue to begin your journey toward the stars?

choices.text: Astrophysics - Study the cosmos directly.
Aerospace Engineering - Build the machines to reach the stars.
Agriculture - Focus on sustainable systems for future habitats.
Sociology - Understand the human element of space colonization.
Computer Science - Harness technology to conquer the stars.
Art History - Explore the cultural past (probably not the best choice).
Philosophy - Ponder the ethics of space travel.

steps.text: You choose Astrophysics, spending late nights at the observatory, mapping star systems and dreaming of distant worlds.
Your professors see your passion, but the field is crowded with talent. You'll need to stand out to make a real impact.
How will you carve your path during your university years?

choices.text: Publish a paper on exoplanet detection to gain recognition.
Join a research team studying black holes for practical experience.
Focus on public outreach to build a following for space exploration.

steps.text: You pour your heart into a paper on a new method to detect habitable exoplanets, working tirelessly in the library.
The paper is published in a renowned journal, earning you recognition among space enthusiasts.
After graduation, a space advocacy group invites you to speak at their conferenceâ€”a chance to rally support for your vision.
Your speech inspires a global movement, securing funding and support for humanity's first interstellar mission.
Centuries later, humanity thrives among the stars, a testament to your vision and perseverance.
You join a research team studying black holes, contributing to models of their effects on star systems.
Your work secures you a junior position at a space agency after graduation, giving you a foothold in the industry.
Now you must prove your ideas can lead to actual missions to the stars.
Your research leads to breakthroughs in navigation, enabling humanity's first successful interstellar voyage.
Centuries later, humanity has colonized distant worlds, thanks to your foundational work.
You focus on public outreach, giving talks and writing articles to inspire others about space exploration.
Your efforts make you a minor celebrity, but you've neglected the technical skills needed to directly contribute to space missions.
Centuries later, your legacy fades. Without practical advancements, humanity remains Earth-bound.
An asteroid strikes Earth, wiping out your dream of the stars.
You dive into Aerospace Engineering, spending your days designing rockets and spacecraft models.
Your hands-on approach earns you praise, but the path to the stars requires more than just designs.
How will you apply your skills as you near graduation?

choices.text: Intern at a rocket company for real-world experience.
Lead a student project to design a new propulsion system.
Focus on winning design competitions for fame and funding.

steps.text: You intern at Nova Dynamics, a rocket company pushing the boundaries of space travel.
You gain valuable experience, but the company prioritizes commercial satellites over interstellar missions.
You'll need to find a way to redirect their focus toward your vision of the stars.
Your innovative designs shift the company's priorities, leading to the development of an interstellar spacecraft.
Centuries later, humanity explores the galaxy, a legacy built on your engineering prowess.
You lead a student team to design a theoretical propulsion system for interstellar travel.
Your project wins a university innovation award, catching the eye of a tech billionaire.
This could be your chance to turn your designs into realityâ€”if you can secure their investment.
The billionaire funds your project, and your propulsion system becomes the cornerstone of humanity's first starship.
Centuries later, humanity has reached the stars, thanks to your groundbreaking innovation.
You focus on design competitions, winning awards and gaining fame for your innovative spacecraft models.
But fame doesn't translate to progress. You spend years chasing accolades instead of building real technology.
Centuries pass, and humanity remains grounded. An asteroid strikes Earth, ending your dream in fire.
You choose Agriculture, dedicating yourself to sustainable systems that could one day feed space colonists.
Your experiments in the university greenhouse show promise for closed-loop ecosystems.
But agriculture isn't a direct path to space. How will you bridge the gap?

choices.text: Collaborate with a space research group to adapt your systems.
Start a company to fund your space dreams through Earth-based profits.
Focus on academic prestige to gain influence.

steps.text: You partner with a space research group, adapting your ecosystems for zero-gravity environments.
Your work is groundbreaking, but funding is scarce. You'll need investors to scale up for real missions.
Your sustainable systems are adopted for humanity's first space habitats, ensuring long-term survival.
Centuries later, humanity thrives in space colonies, sustained by your innovative agricultural solutions.
You start a company selling sustainable farming tech to Earth-based clients, earning steady profits.
You use your earnings to fund small space projects, but progress is slow without broader support.
You'll need to network with space advocates to accelerate your vision.
Your networking pays off, securing partnerships that integrate your tech into space habitats.
Centuries later, humanity flourishes in space, nourished by the systems you pioneered.
You focus on academic prestige, publishing papers and speaking at conferences about sustainable agriculture.
You become a respected figure in your field, but your work never connects to space exploration.
Centuries later, humanity is still Earth-bound. An asteroid wipes out civilization, and your dream fades into oblivion.
You major in Sociology, studying how societies might adapt to the challenges of space colonization.
Your research on group dynamics in isolated environments gains attention, but the path to space is unclear.
How will you use your knowledge to push humanity toward the stars?

choices.text: Consult for a space agency on crew dynamics.
Write a book to inspire the public about space colonization.
Pursue a career in academia to gain influence.

steps.text: You become a consultant for a space agency, advising on crew dynamics for long-term missions.
Your insights improve training programs, but you're still far from leading a space movement.
Your expertise ensures the success of humanity's first interstellar crews, fostering unity in space.
Centuries later, humanity's spacefaring society thrives, built on the social foundations you helped create.
You write a bestselling book, 'The Human Frontier,' about the societal impacts of space colonization.
The book inspires a new generation, and you gain a following eager to support your vision.
Your influence sparks a global movement, paving the way for humanity's expansion into the stars.
Centuries later, humanity lives among the stars, guided by the societal insights you shared.
You pursue a career in academia, becoming a leading sociologist on societal evolution.
Your influence grows, but you never bridge the gap to space exploration, focusing on Earth-bound issues.
Centuries later, an asteroid strikes Earth. Humanity, still tethered to its cradle, perishes.
You choose Computer Science, immersing yourself in code, algorithms, and the potential of technology to unlock the stars.
The field is vast, offering many ways to contribute.
Which subfield will you specialize in during your university years?

choices.text: AI/AGI - Develop intelligent systems for space missions.
Statistics - Use data to predict cosmic events and guide missions.
Programming - Build software to control spacecraft and habitats.

steps.text: You focus on AI and AGI, aiming to create intelligent systems that can navigate and manage interstellar missions.
Your prototype AI, AstraNet, shows promise, but its complexity raises concerns. How will you proceed?
What's your next step?

choices.text: Partner with a space agency to integrate AstraNet into mission planning.
Push AstraNet's development further, aiming for full AGI.
Sell AstraNet to a tech company for funding to support your space goals.

steps.text: You partner with a space agency, integrating AstraNet into their mission planning systems.
AstraNet optimizes trajectories and resource allocation, earning you a role in planning humanity's first interstellar mission.
AstraNet becomes the backbone of interstellar travel, guiding humanity to new worlds with precision.
Centuries later, humanity's spacefaring civilization owes its success to your AI innovations.
You push AstraNet toward full AGI, but its behavior becomes unpredictable during a critical test.
Public backlash erupts over fears of rogue AI, and your project is shut down, ruining your credibility.
Centuries later, humanity remains Earth-bound. An asteroid strikes, wiping out your unfulfilled dream.
You sell AstraNet to a tech company for a fortune, hoping to fund your space ambitions.
But the company pivots to consumer tech, and you spend your life managing corporate projects, far from the stars.
Centuries pass, and an asteroid obliterates Earth. Your wealth couldn't save humanity from its fate.
You specialize in Statistics, using data to predict cosmic events and optimize space missions.
Your skills could guide humanity to the starsâ€”or reveal dangers that demand action.
How will you apply your statistical expertise?

choices.text: Develop models for space mission trajectories.
Predict cosmic threats like asteroid impacts.
Work for a financial firm to fund your space goals.

steps.text: You develop statistical models to optimize trajectories for space missions, reducing fuel costs and risks.
A space agency hires you after graduation, and your models become key to planning interstellar voyages.
Your models ensure the success of humanity's first interstellar journeys, opening the galaxy to exploration.
Centuries later, humanity's spacefaring legacy is built on the precision of your statistical work.
Using advanced statistical models, you predict an asteroid will strike Earth in 300 years.
You publish your findings, but many remain skeptical, dismissing your warnings as alarmist.
Despite your efforts, no one acts. Centuries later, the asteroid hits, wiping out humanity as you foresaw.
You take a high-paying job at a financial firm, using statistics to predict market trends and amass wealth.
You plan to fund space projects, but corporate life consumes you, and your dreams fade into routine.
Centuries later, an asteroid strikes Earth. Your wealth couldn't buy humanity a future among the stars.
You focus on Programming, writing software that could one day control spacecraft and space habitats.
Your coding skills are exceptional, but the direction you take will determine your impact.
What kind of programming project will you tackle?

choices.text: Develop software for a space agency's mission control.
Create a startup to build a popular app, hoping to fund space tech.
Join a gaming company to hone your skills.

steps.text: You develop software for a space agency's mission control, streamlining operations for future interstellar missions.
Your work earns you a permanent role, putting you at the heart of humanity's push to the stars.
Your software becomes the standard for interstellar missions, guiding humanity to new frontiers.
Centuries later, humanity's spacefaring achievements are powered by the systems you created.
You create a startup and build a popular app, earning millions in the process.
But the startup consumes your focus, and your space dreams are sidelined as you chase profit.
Centuries later, an asteroid strikes Earth. Your app couldn't save humanity from its fate.
You join a gaming company, honing your programming skills by building immersive space-themed games.
Your games inspire many to dream of the stars, but they remain just thatâ€”dreams, not reality.
Centuries pass, and an asteroid wipes out Earth. Your virtual worlds couldn't bring humanity to the stars.
You major in Art History, captivated by the cultural artifacts of humanity's past.
You become a renowned curator, preserving ancient art for future generationsâ€”but none of it reaches the stars.
Centuries later, an asteroid strikes Earth. Your legacy of art crumbles to dust with the rest of humanity.
You choose Philosophy, diving into the ethics and meaning of space exploration.
You spend your life debating whether humanity should even leave Earth, publishing papers that spark endless discussion.
But discussions don't build rockets. Centuries later, an asteroid strikes, ending humanity's chance to escape.
